findings.summary: Wrenfold outperforms Fennick-Base on the unseen Banking and Travel test sets by 1.5 and 1.5 percentage points in macro-F1, respectively.
findings.scope: Unseen test sets of Banking and Travel domains, macro-F1, mean over 5 seeds.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; differences are descriptive only.

findings.summary: The evidence does not support generalization beyond the Banking and Travel domains, as no other domains were evaluated.
findings.scope: Only Banking and Travel domains in the Harrowgate corpus.

findings.summary: Both Wrenfold and Fennick-Base substantially outperform the Keyword-SVM reference on both domains, with Wrenfold leading by 8.9 and 8.9 percentage points respectively.
findings.scope: Unseen test sets of Banking and Travel, macro-F1.

sentences.text: On the unseen Banking and Travel test sets, Wrenfold achieved macro-F1 scores of 93.1% and 92.4%, respectively, outperforming Fennick-Base by 1.5 percentage points in each domain.
However, because no statistical tests were reported, these differences are descriptive only and cannot be interpreted as significant.
The evaluation was limited to the Banking and Travel domains, so the results do not provide evidence that Wrenfold's advantage generalizes to other domains.
Both neural models substantially outperformed the Keyword-SVM reference, with Wrenfold leading by 8.9 percentage points on each domain.
